analysis: Two files changed. (1) ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift line 249: the new MLXOpenAIServiceError case .responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens is mapped to HTTP 422, the same status as invalidResponseFormatOutput. This is a status-code mapping inside the closed InferenceFailure contract. The sanitizedInferenceFailure path (lines 15-34) is unchanged: no raw error strings are emitted. inferenceFailureCode falls through the statusCode switch (400/422 -> .invalidRequest) and boundedInferenceErrorReason returns nil for this error, so no new wire vocabulary or data exposure is introduced. Impact is only on coordinator failover/retry semantics, where a 422 follows the normal bounded path rather than a 5xx provider-fault class. That is a behavioral choice, not a security regression. I could not verify the enum case definition in MLXLMServer (outside the supplied evidence); a missing case would break compilation (the switch is exhaustive), not weaken security. (2) EngineV2BridgeTests.swift: test-only changes. They add a decodeTable to StubTokenizer, a stopStringScope parameter on makeBridge, and tests for scoped stop-string matching (gpt-oss harmony and reasoning scopes). The tests exercise stop-sequence reporting only; no production code is touched, and no cache, key, attestation or authorization surface changes. The underlying stop-scope production code (EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence, ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope) is not in this batch, so its correctness is unexamined here. No findings. Threat-model entries T-041, T-008 and the rest are unaffected.
